I.def.15: A circle is a plane figure contained by one line such that all the straight lines falling upon it from one point among those lying within the figure are equal to one another.
I.post.1: To draw a straight line from any point to any point.
I.post.2: To produce a finite straight line continuously in a straight line.
I.post.3: To describe a circle with any centre and distance.
I.post.4: That all right angles are equal to one another.
I.post.5: That, if a straight line falling on two straight lines make the interior angles on the same side less than two right angles, the two straight lines, if produced indefinitely, meet…
I.cn.1: Things which are equal to the same thing are also equal to one another.
I.cn.2: If equals be added to equals, the wholes are equal.
I.cn.3: If equals be subtracted from equals, the remainders are equal.
I.cn.4: Things which coincide with one another are equal to one another.
I.1: On a given finite straight line to construct an equilateral triangle.
I.2: To place at a given point (as an extremity) a straight line equal to a given straight line.
I.3: Given two unequal straight lines, to cut off from the greater a straight line equal to the less.

I.11: To draw a straight line at right angles to a given straight line from a given point on it.
I.13: If a straight line set up on a straight line make angles, it will make either two right angles or angles equal to two right angles.
I.15: If two straight lines cut one another, they make the vertical angles equal to one another.
